text:
saman.sales: CorpX returned the security questionnaire. Two net questions: 1) Which topology should we recommend for their POC (VPC Peering vs PrivateLink)? 2) Exact firewall/egress guidance + short cost note for RFP. Need a short, copy-paste answer.

devin.sre: Short answer: PrivateLink for customer-isolated POC traffic. It avoids cross-account route injection and makes allowlisting straightforward. Use peering only if they require low-level VPC routing between their workloads and our connector (rare for multi-tenant POCs).

chris.platform: Adding operational detail: PrivateLink (interface endpoint) means customer creates ENIs in their subnet with private IPs we present. They allow outbound TCP/443 to those IPs and we're reachable over TLS. No route propagation from our side, no route tables to manage.

olivia.sec: For the RFP snippet, they asked for exact firewall entries and how to validate endpoints. Paste this: 
```
Firewall allowlist (PrivateLink POC):
- Protocol: TCP
- Port: 443
- Destination: list of interface endpoint private IPs (we will supply 3-4 per region before handoff)
- Optional: UDP 123 to your NTP server if host time sync is enforced
Validation steps:
- Validate server cert chain + SAN matches "redwood-inference.internal" (we provide cert thumbprint)
- Use SNI and cert pinning where your proxy allows
- For Private Deploy connector: enable mTLS (we'll provide client certs)
```

saman.sales: Nice. They also have a corporate egress proxy and asked if routing through that changes costs or breaks authentication.

devin.sre: Two important effects: 1) If traffic goes via their egress proxy (all external TLS proxied/inspected), that proxy will SNAT and our service will see proxy IPs, which removes per-customer source IP preservation unless they preserve original src via X-Forwarded-For and we trust it (not recommended for auth). 2) TLS-inspection can break mTLS and mutual certificate verification. Recommend proxy passthrough for any connectors doing mTLS, or configuring the proxy to allow TLS passthrough for our endpoint FQDNs.

chris.platform: Cost note: interface endpoints incur AWS endpoint charges (and cross-AZ data transfer) billed to the customer. Egress via their public NAT/Internet will show up as normal cloud egress on their bill. If you want a single line for the RFP: "We recommend PrivateLink for POC isolation. Customers incur AWS interface endpoint costs; public NAT egress is billed by the cloud provider. Redwoodcan include estimated data transfer in Dedicated/Private quotes on request."

olivia.sec: Add a short paragraph about peering risks: 
Peering caveat: VPC peering exposes route-level access; the peer can reach all allowed subnets per route table. For strict network isolation and least-privilege allowlisting, use PrivateLink.

devin.sre: Operational checklist to send to customer (pasteable): 
```
POC network checklist:
1) Choose topology: PRIVATELINK (recommended) or VPC PEERING (only if needed)
2) Create interface endpoint(s) in your VPC and share private IPs with Redwood
3) Add outbound firewall rule: TCP 443 -> provided IPs
4) If using egress proxy: enable TLS passthrough to endpoint FQDNs or allow our certs through inspector
5) Provide contact for ATO/network diagram generation
6) Optionally enable mTLS for connector auth (requires cert exchange)
7) For load tests: ensure NAT gateway has sufficient ephemeral ports or use multiple NATs/ALBs to avoid SNAT exhaustion
```

infra-bot: Created infra ticket INF-8001 to provision PrivateLink endpoints and return IP list. Will post when ready.

saman.sales: Perfect. Also customer asked about SNAT port exhaustion mitigation steps 1k ports per NAT. Can we give a short note?

devin.sre: Sure: If >10k concurrent connections expected during load tests, recommend: (a) use multiple NAT gateway IPs or NAT instances with multiple ENIs, (b) use HTTP/2 or connection reuse to reduce concurrent sockets, (c) test with distributed load to validate ephemeral port limits. We'll share our load-to-concurrency guidelines once we know expected RPS.

olivia.sec: I'll attach SOC2 + KMS/BYOK FAQ in the email. Also: for the questionnaire item about cert validation, include that we publish cert thumbprints and recommend customers verify the chain during onboarding.

saman.sales: Thanks everyone. I'll assemble a single response for CorpX with: recommended topology, firewall snippet, RFP cost line, and operational checklist. @infra-bot ping me when INF-8001 is done.

infra-bot: INF-8001 updated: provisioning started. Will post endpoint IPs to this thread (reaction :rocket:).
